# Inferra

> Inferra is the Git-native cloud: a PaaS that builds APIs, web apps and background workers from GitHub pushes with Cloud Native Buildpacks and runs them with managed Postgres, a Redis-compatible Valkey cache and S3 buckets.

Teams write the code; Inferra runs the servers, clusters, builds, HTTPS, patching, restarts, rolling deploys, logs and metrics. Website: https://inferralab.com. Facts below were reviewed on 2026-10-10.

## Key facts
- Deploys only through Git pushes. One file in the repository, `.inferra/org.yaml`, maps branches to spaces (production, staging, previews) and declares apps and their managed services. Results appear as GitHub commit statuses.
- Builds from source with Cloud Native Buildpacks, no Dockerfile: Node.js, Python, Go, Java, Ruby, PHP, .NET, static sites and Procfile apps.
- Web apps and long-running background workers. An app with a `command` and no `port` is a worker: no address or health check, it keeps running. Services and workers are long-running processes, not time-limited functions.
- Managed Postgres (7-day backup window), Redis-compatible Valkey cache and S3 buckets. A database or cache accepts connections only from the apps bound to it in `org.yaml`.
- Previews: pushing a branch that matches the preview pattern creates a copy of the apps in the preview space, apart from production, with the preview space's own services. Deleting the branch removes the copy. Each copy counts toward the app limit.
- Every app on every plan, including Free, runs in a gVisor sandbox. Outbound access is the same on every plan: public destinations on any port, never private ranges or cloud metadata.
- Pricing is flat: Free (7-day trial), Pro $20/month, Team $99/month. Reaching a plan limit stops the next push; nothing is added to the bill automatically.
- The `inferra` CLI inspects and operates (logs, metrics, exec, rollback, promote); it never deploys source.

## Preview status
- The platform is in preview. Sign-in and the API currently run on the development environment (api.dev.inferralab.com).
- Coming soon, not available yet: custom domains and the hosted MCP server for AI assistants.
- `inferra init --secret NAME` (send only listed secrets from GitHub) needs CLI 0.4.0-rc.17 or later; otherwise set secret values in the dashboard.

## Getting started
- [Your first deployment](https://inferralab.com/setup/): install the GitHub App, commit `.inferra/org.yaml`, push, read the commit status, add Postgres.
- [Download the CLI](https://inferralab.com/download/): macOS, Linux and Windows builds with SHA-256 checksums.
- [Pricing and plan limits](https://inferralab.com/#pricing)

## Reference
- [Documentation](https://inferralab.com/docs/)
- [org.yaml reference](https://inferralab.com/docs/org-yaml/): every accepted field, workers, previews, services, validation rules.
- [CLI reference](https://inferralab.com/docs/cli/): logs, metrics, instances, rollback and promotion.
- [Adding SSO to your app](https://inferralab.com/docs/sso/): OAuth/OpenID Connect, SAML and LDAPS sign-in inside your app.
- [Release notes](https://inferralab.com/changelog/)

## Compare
- [Inferra vs Vercel, Heroku, Render, Railway and Fly.io](https://inferralab.com/compare/): pricing, workers, Postgres, previews and isolation, with official sources, verified 2026-10-10.

## Security
- [Security and data handling](https://inferralab.com/security/): gVisor isolation, network rules, write-only secrets, deletion and backup retention.
- [Website privacy](https://inferralab.com/privacy/): no website analytics today.

## Planned
- [MCP server (coming soon)](https://inferralab.com/mcp/): read-only troubleshooting for assistants; configuration changes only as pull requests to `org.yaml`.
- [Demo](https://inferralab.com/demo/): an API, a worker and Postgres deployed from the public inferra-AI/inferra-demo repository.
